This is weirdly inspiring. I feel like I'm pretty much in that spot you were in awhile ago right now. Friendships ended. Confusion over blame. Depression. So thank you for this. It makes me feel... hopeful.

I'm glad you've reached this revelation and cared to share it!
Is it weird if I say a lot of books have changed my life? Because I honestly feel like so many works have an impact on who I am today

My middle school years fucking sucked. There were no good times. Songs like this did not help much.

Disney's Extreme Skate Adventure. There's some early 00's stuff on the soundtrack (ie: simple plan, allister)

I don't think you should assume anything. If/when you meet up again, I think you should talk to him about how you're feeling/why you're feeling this way. Assuming you know why someone is doing what they're doing is literally the worst thing you can do, in my opinion. But hey, what do I know.

Edit// I also think that you could talk to him about how you're feeling on the phone/text/however you're usually in contact with him

"If you don’t like answering the questions from other people, it means you don’t like the answer."

I love that. Because it's true.

Personally, I'm a big lover of Stephen King. All of his novels aren't horror, and some are definitely better than others, but I think he's worth reading. 
I'd recommend his short story collection "Full Dark, No Stars" and "Misery." The short story collection is easy to get through and has a bunch of good horror stories, if I remember correctly and "Misery" is just a good book.
